Wim Wenders: Looking back on the road ahead

I was introduced to Wim Wenders with Alice in the Cities followed by The Goalies Anxiety at the Penalty Kick. I have seen nearly everything he has made. He is the best of all the German new wave directors.

Edit: corrected spelling of surname

I've only been aware of Wenders since a couple of years ago and have some of his films that I need to get around to watching. So far my only experience with the German new wave has been with Fassbinder.

A few weeks ago I found out about Until the End of the World which looks to have a cyberpunk vibe so that would be right up my alley, hopefully the directors cut gets a Blu-ray release as it looks visually impressive.

I like Until the End of the World. It stars two favorite actors, Max von Sydow and Jeane Moreau and it has a great soundtrack. It received lukewarm reviews at the time, but that doesn't matter if you really like an artist. I recommend it.

To be honest, I really like everything he has done up to Million Dollar Hotel. His subsequent movies have not held my interest, with the exception of Buena Vista Cafe, which is more of a documentary on the Cuban Jazz scene.

Two other recommendations: Paris, Texas, and Wings of Desire. The latter was remade as City of Angels, which I didn't like as much as Wenders original.

I've seen alot of Fassbinder's films. Some I like Some I dont. He tended to film too quickly so the quality and interest level seems inconsistent to me. He is certainly one of the more important directors of the German New Wave, but not one of my favorites in spite of how many films I've seen of his. I do recommend "The Third Generation," though. Stay away from World on a Wire. Long, slow, and stagnant. Too many talking heads saying very little of interest. Not much going for it visually either in spite of it being a science fiction film.
I loved Wim Wenders. I'm sure the new germans will really get into him in a big way.
